newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RBNZ forecasts assume TWI constant at 65.0.
newsitem.headline: RBNZ forecasts assume TWI constant at 65.0.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand said on Friday that inflation forecasts in its six monthly economic projections assumed the New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index (TWI) to remain constant at 65.0 throughout the forecast period.
The TWI assumption is a departure from previous forecasts.
In June, the bank's forecasts had assumed the average value of the TWI would rise 1.7 percent annually to reach 66.7 by March 1999 from a starting point of 64.0 during the September 1996 quarter.
The TWI was 65.8 at 7.00 a.m. (1900 gmt) on Friday morning.
